courseReview.finding: Required Year-1 formation; not justified as a concept-generated elective.
Enriched AI-focused profile supports the digital-society strand. Correct shared modal retained and actually rechecked.
Micro/macro foundations support the evidenced cultural-economics purpose; no dedicated creative-market syllabus is claimed.
Producer/consumer choice, market structure and regulation give a specific economic framework; cultural applications remain a comparator difference.
Public goods, spending, externalities and government intervention support public value/funding questions; not specialist cultural-industry analysis.
Marketing strategy and consumer engagement support audience/market study; cultural marketing is not the entire course.
Digital strategy and organisational innovation implement the digital-change strand; not a cultural-sector futures syllabus.
Applied customer-opinion data collection and analysis supplies market/audience inquiry, without pretending it is a cultural-management research workshop.
Venture ideation, validation and social entrepreneurship implement the creative-enterprise direction; no compulsory arts startup assignment is asserted.
Actual research design, descriptive/inferential statistics and group inquiry; stronger than a generic transferable-skills justification.
Organisational culture, groups, leadership and change support management; external cultural-financing and production scope remains a gap.
Enriched philosophical and psychological AI ethics supports the digital-society strand. Stale modal focus replaced with a faithful concise profile paraphrase and source provenance.
Cleaning, manipulating and visualising tables/text/spatial data plus a project support cultural/media research; no full statistics/SPSS claim.
Legal systems, public/private law, case reasoning and justice support the institutional public-life purpose.
Modern political/economic/cultural developments and decolonisation give defined historical substance to the society route.
Gendered histories and storytelling through cultural forms provide a specific identity/culture relationship; American scope should remain clear.
Theories and histories of empire contribute power/institutional formation; do not imply dedicated arts policy.
Indigenous stories, artistic expression, cultural resistance and regeneration directly support the culture/public-life purpose.
Historical/philosophical/legal rights and liberty/equality cases support public-life questions; no dedicated arts-rights curriculum is claimed.
Historical philosophical problems of knowledge, responsibility and freedom support the philosophy/modernity strand; avoid generic culture-context justification.
Ethical theory, historical injustice, equality and future generations support public choices in the society route.
EU public authority, legislative dossiers and interest-group influence support institutional public life; cultural-policy component remains unmatched.
Conflict, identity-based grievances, reconciliation and civil-society action support the explicitly evidenced polarisation/public-life interest.
Social theory and analysis of institutions/race/gender support sociological cultural inquiry; not a specialised arts-sociology sequence.
Meaning, positionality, qualitative research design/data/interpretation directly support inquiry into culture and social life.
Modernity, colonial responses and social theory support the programme’s culture/society relationship.
Movements, feminism, anti-colonialism and environmental justice support collective/public life; not arts-and-health provision.
Civil society, public sphere, solidarity, decolonial critique and CSO inquiry support society/media/public life. Final concepts explicitly avoid specialist cultural-sociology coverage.
Rhetorical discourse and composition across public/media settings support the communication route.
Stylistics, linguistic choices and literary/nonfiction meaning directly support cultural/media interpretation.
Ethical persuasion and applied institutional communication support the societal/media communication direction; not a claim that all assignments concern cultural organisations.
Poetry, performance and experimental creative meaning-making provide actual cultural/creative study.
Western visual art history, interpretation and institutions establish core art/culture study.
Making, material culture and religious/social/gendered identities provide specific archaeological-cultural inquiry, not a substitute for contemporary heritage institutions.
African art, colonial collecting and museum/repatriation debates directly support heritage and institutional cultural value.
Modern art, curating, museums and exhibitions directly support art/heritage institutions.
Available description establishes art historiography and interpretation; no outline or supervised empirical thesis is inferred.
Practical criticism, genre and constructed literary value directly support interpretation.
Chronological literary works and representations of social life support cultural history and interpretation.
Adaptation and formal film/text analysis directly implement the media-cultural strand.
Primarily film history/form/analysis with a shorter wider-media introduction; preserve that relative emphasis in claims.
Material/pre-digital media histories and knowledge circulation provide substantive cultural media study.
American mainstream narratives and representation provide a specific television/platform/identity strand, not general technical platform training.
Visual/audiovisual environmental representation and postcolonial/Indigenous media support the climate/cultural question.
American race, cultural expression and research-based podcast work support representation and public memory.
Documentary history, ethics/aesthetics and a short production implement the media/culture concept; no full independent thesis is inferred.

Renaissance art, trade, colonisation and cross-cultural artistic exchange directly implement the retained art-history and society concept. Current description-only evidence supports this bounded contribution; no richer syllabus is invented. Offered 2029h1, formal prerequisite NONE.

courseReview.finding: Required Year-1 formation; not justified as a concept-generated elective.
AI-driven organisational/economic change supports the digital-society route; enriched profile supports selection but the modal uses stale base copy.
Micro/macro foundations support the evidenced cultural-economics purpose; no dedicated creative-market syllabus is claimed.
Producer/consumer choice, market structure and regulation give a specific economic framework; cultural applications remain a comparator difference.
Public goods, spending, externalities and government intervention support public value/funding questions; not specialist cultural-industry analysis.
Marketing strategy and consumer engagement support audience/market study; cultural marketing is not the entire course.
Digital strategy and organisational innovation implement the digital-change strand; not a cultural-sector futures syllabus.
Applied customer-opinion data collection and analysis supplies market/audience inquiry, without pretending it is a cultural-management research workshop.
Venture ideation, validation and social entrepreneurship implement the creative-enterprise direction; no compulsory arts startup assignment is asserted.
Actual research design, descriptive/inferential statistics and group inquiry; stronger than a generic transferable-skills justification.
Organisational culture, groups, leadership and change support management; external cultural-financing and production scope remains a gap.
Bias, responsibility, agency and AI governance support digital media/society; base description has older emphasis, so prefer enriched profile in revised claims.
Cleaning, manipulating and visualising tables/text/spatial data plus a project support cultural/media research; no full statistics/SPSS claim.
Legal systems, public/private law, case reasoning and justice support the institutional public-life purpose.
Modern political/economic/cultural developments and decolonisation give defined historical substance to the society route.
Gendered histories and storytelling through cultural forms provide a specific identity/culture relationship; American scope should remain clear.
Theories and histories of empire contribute power/institutional formation; do not imply dedicated arts policy.
Indigenous stories, artistic expression, cultural resistance and regeneration directly support the culture/public-life purpose.
Historical/philosophical/legal rights and liberty/equality cases support public-life questions; no dedicated arts-rights curriculum is claimed.
Historical philosophical problems of knowledge, responsibility and freedom support the philosophy/modernity strand; avoid generic culture-context justification.
Ethical theory, historical injustice, equality and future generations support public choices in the society route.
EU public authority, legislative dossiers and interest-group influence support institutional public life; cultural-policy component remains unmatched.
Conflict, identity-based grievances, reconciliation and civil-society action support the explicitly evidenced polarisation/public-life interest.
Social theory and analysis of institutions/race/gender support sociological cultural inquiry; not a specialised arts-sociology sequence.
Meaning, positionality, qualitative research design/data/interpretation directly support inquiry into culture and social life.
Modernity, colonial responses and social theory support the programme’s culture/society relationship.
Movements, feminism, anti-colonialism and environmental justice support collective/public life; not arts-and-health provision.
Civil/public sphere, solidarity, decolonial critique and CSO inquiry support society/media/public life; dedicated cultural-sociology wording overstates the actual focus.
Rhetorical discourse and composition across public/media settings support the communication route.
Stylistics, linguistic choices and literary/nonfiction meaning directly support cultural/media interpretation.

Specific primary-school rhetoric/debate teaching project, mainly in Dutch. Existing cultural-public-communication rationale needs a concrete academic relationship to the established first concept or a bounded replacement.
Ethical persuasion and applied institutional communication support the societal/media communication direction; not a claim that all assignments concern cultural organisations.
Poetry, performance and experimental creative meaning-making provide actual cultural/creative study.
Western visual art history, interpretation and institutions establish core art/culture study.
Making, material culture and religious/social/gendered identities provide specific archaeological-cultural inquiry, not a substitute for contemporary heritage institutions.
African art, colonial collecting and museum/repatriation debates directly support heritage and institutional cultural value.
Modern art, curating, museums and exhibitions directly support art/heritage institutions.
Available description establishes art historiography and interpretation; no outline or supervised empirical thesis is inferred.
Practical criticism, genre and constructed literary value directly support interpretation.
Chronological literary works and representations of social life support cultural history and interpretation.
Adaptation and formal film/text analysis directly implement the media-cultural strand.
Primarily film history/form/analysis with a shorter wider-media introduction; preserve that relative emphasis in claims.
Material/pre-digital media histories and knowledge circulation provide substantive cultural media study.
American mainstream narratives and representation provide a specific television/platform/identity strand, not general technical platform training.
Visual/audiovisual environmental representation and postcolonial/Indigenous media support the climate/cultural question.
American race, cultural expression and research-based podcast work support representation and public memory.
Documentary history, ethics/aesthetics and a short production implement the media/culture concept; no full independent thesis is inferred.
